viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
ICE Agents and Deputies Pull Suspected Illegal Alien Alberto Lira Razo Out of His Van in Hamilton, Ohio

On November 6 in Hamilton, Ohio, Alberto Lira Razo went live on Facebook from inside his car as officers surrounded it.  An agent at his window is wearing a vest marked ICE with a DHS patch.

Razo told the deputy to "Break it. Break it." and the deputy did exactly that.

His daughter, Loudmouth Lupe, filmed from outside.  Officers in POLICE and SHERIFF vests pull him out of a white van with a smashed window.

Then they shove and body-block her while she's filming.  She can be heard saying, "Get off of me, I am a child!"

On the tape, she says they tased and punched her dad.  Neither is shown in either video.

He's reportedly 38 and was booked on an ICE hold.  No agency has released a statement, and no charges have been announced.

Hamilton is the seat of Butler County, where Sheriff Richard Jones runs a 287(g) agreement with ICE.  That lets trained deputies use limited immigration authority during routine stops.

Jones has said ICE trained 44 of his deputies.  Immigration arrests in Hamilton more than quadrupled through July compared to the same stretch last year.
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_zh:
ICE 特工和副手在俄亥俄州汉密尔顿将疑似非法外国人阿尔贝托·里拉·拉佐 (Alberto Lira Razo) 从他的货车中拉出来

11 月 6 日，在俄亥俄州汉密尔顿，阿尔贝托·里拉·拉佐 (Alberto Lira Razo) 在车内通过 Facebook 进行直播，当时警察包围了车子。 一名特工站在窗口，穿着一件带有 ICE 标记和 DHS 补丁的背心。

拉佐告诉副警长“打破它。打破它。”副手正是这样做的。

他的女儿劳德茅斯·卢佩 (Loudmouth Lupe) 在外面拍摄。 身着警察和警长背心的警察将他从一辆窗户被砸碎的白色货车中拉出来。

然后他们在她拍摄时推搡并用身体挡住她。 可以听到她说：“放开我，我还是个孩子！”

在录音中，她说他们殴打了她的父亲。 两个视频中都没有显示。

据报道，他今年 38 岁，并被 ICE 拘留。 没有机构发表声明，也没有宣布任何指控。

汉密尔顿是巴特勒县的县治，治安官理查德·琼斯 (Richard Jones) 与 ICE 签订了 287(g) 协议。 这使得训练有素的警员在例行停留期间可以使用有限的移民权力。

琼斯表示，ICE 培训了 44 名副手。 与去年同期相比，7 月份汉密尔顿逮捕的移民人数增加了四倍多。

viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
AI has made it incredibly easy to build an app, but choosing the right architecture is still a different skill.

Postgres is a great default, but it isn't the answer to every problem. Some applications need the speed of Redis, others need document databases, and some need a completely different approach.

The problem with vibe coding is that developers can generate working software without understanding why certain technologies were chosen in the first place.

Being able to build an app with Claude is impressive. Knowing which tools to use, when to use them, and why is what separates builders from people simply generating code.
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_zh:
人工智能使构建应用程序变得异常容易，但选择正确的架构仍然是一项不同的技能。

Postgres 是一个很好的默认设置，但它并不能解决所有问题。有些应用程序需要 Redis 的速度，有些应用程序需要文档数据库，有些则需要完全不同的方法。

Vibe 编码的问题在于，开发人员可以在不了解为什么选择某些技术的情况下生成工作软件。

能够与 Claude 一起构建应用程序令人印象深刻。知道使用哪些工具、何时使用以及为什么使用这些工具，是构建者与简单生成代码的人的区别。

Source: https://t.co/RgsNkb5WjL

In 2020, Senators @tedcruz, @SenTomCotton, and then Senator @GovBraun Mike Braun, who is the current Governor of Indiana, called on the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) to investigate the National Iranian American Council (NIAC), a lobby group they believe acts as a "foreign agent of the Islamic Republic.”

Trita likely was going to be deported, until he and his colleagues at Quincy allegedly called in a favor to a very senior  official at the White House. 

Any wild guesses who that is? 🤔 

Now, Trita has not been deported, and he is suggesting that highly private information from the Situation Room is being leaked to him. 

@SecRubio this would be the perfect time before the Democrats take over in January for you to revoke Trita Parsi’s visa and have him removed from our country. 

Again, I flagged all of this for the WH over 6 months ago.

It won’t end well. 

Deport Trita Parsi!

@SecRubio，这将是民主党一月份上台之前撤销 Trita Parsi 签证并将他驱逐出我国的最佳时机。

viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
Don’t just trust an AI’s answer verify how it was generated.

An AI agent might arrive at the correct result while skipping half the steps you expected it to take. For a simple query, that might not matter. @primus_labs 

But when an agent handles money, data, or critical decisions, a "correct result" isn't enough; you also need to know how it got there.

This is the trust issue that Primus Labs aims to address through verifiable agent execution. 

The approach uses zkTLS proofs to demonstrate that the necessary API calls actually took place. 

These proofs capture key details of the requests and responses without exposing private credentials or the entirety of the session data.

Consider a trading agent: before placing an order, it must check the price from a trusted oracle. 

Typically, you would simply have to take the agent’s word that it did so. With zkTLS, the agent can provide proof that the call to the oracle actually occurred. 

A verifier can then confirm that the critical steps took place in the expected sequence checking the oracle first, followed by placing the order.

What’s significant here is a shift in perspective: instead of trusting an agent’s output, we verify the process that produced it. 

Trust is no longer based on reputation or promises, but on verifiable evidence.

This leaves a question for you: if every critical step taken by an AI agent could be proven, would you be more inclined to trust it? @primus_labs 

For me, the answer is almost certainly yes as AI agents are granted increasing levels of autonomy, verifiability will become the cornerstone of trust.
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_zh:
不要只相信人工智能的答案，验证它是如何生成的。

人工智能代理可能会跳过您预期要执行的一半步骤，从而得出正确的结果。对于简单的查询，这可能并不重要。 @primus_labs

但是，当代理处理资金、数据或关键决策时，“正确的结果”是不够的；还需要有“正确的结果”。你还需要知道它是如何到达那里的。

这是 Primus Labs 旨在通过可验证的代理执行来解决的信任问题。

该方法使用 zkTLS 证明来证明必要的 API 调用确实发生了。

这些证明捕获请求和响应的关键细节，而不会暴露私人凭证或整个会话数据。

考虑一个交易代理：在下订单之前，它必须检查来自可信预言机的价格。

通常情况下，您只需相信代理人的话即可。通过 zkTLS，代理可以提供对预言机的调用实际发生的证据。

然后，验证者可以首先检查预言机，然后下订单，以确认关键步骤按照预期顺序发生。

这里重要的是视角的转变：我们不再信任代理的输出，而是验证产生它的过程。

信任不再基于声誉或承诺，而是基于可验证的证据。

这给你留下了一个问题：如果人工智能代理采取的每一个关键步骤都可以被证明，你会更倾向于信任它吗？ @primus_labs

对我来说，答案几乎肯定是肯定的，随着人工智能代理被授予越来越多的自主权，可验证性将成为信任的基石。

top_three.content_snippet:
A Google Research AI can detect signs of high blood pressure using a regular smartwatch, with no blood pressure cuff needed for calibration. The AI relies on two sensors already built into modern watches—a pulse sensor and a motion sensor—according to a Google blog post. The study was published in Nature.

A neural network learned from nearly 500,000 hours of sensor data by comparing short segments and figuring out which ones belonged to the same person, picking up typical pulse and heartbeat pa
top_three.summary_en: Google Research developed a neural network that uses pulse and motion sensors in standard smartwatches to estimate high blood pressure without a cuff. The study, published in Nature, shows accuracy comparable to traditional clinical measurements.

news.title: Investigation: some Chinese firms approved by the US Commerce Department to handle Nvidia's H200 chips have empty offices and ties to firms under sanctions (New York Times)
news.title_en: Investigation: some Chinese firms approved by the US Commerce Department to handle Nvidia's H200 chips have empty offices and ties to firms under sanctions (New York Times)
news.author: New York Times
news.content_snippet: The Commerce Department has approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia's H200 chips, some of which have ties to firms under sanctions over national security.
news.summary_en: The US Commerce Department previously approved Chinese companies to import Nvidia H200 chips, but investigations reveal some firms have empty offices and links to sanctioned entities. This discovery has sparked intense scrutiny over the efficacy and vetting rigor of US semiconductor export controls.

[Perspective & Impact] Exposure of critical regulatory gaps in export controls.

news.title: State propaganda in some Chinese AI models is only "a thin layer" that fine-tuning can strip away
news.title_en: State propaganda in some Chinese AI models is only "a thin layer" that fine-tuning can strip away
news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
Nous Research fine-tuned Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B on 53 million tokens to strip out Chinese state propaganda. The resulting model, Arete-27B, drops its propaganda rate from 22 percent to under one percent while keeping general capabilities intact.

Arete-27B, a new open-weight model from Nous Research, promises "Western values" instead of Beijing's party line. The US startup, best known for its open-source agent Hermes, fine-tuned Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B to get there.

According to Nous, Chinese open
news.summary_en: US startup Nous Research fine-tuned Alibaba's Qwen2.5-27B model to create a new version called Arete-27B. By injecting specific datasets, the team reduced the original model's propaganda output rate from 22% to under 1%, aiming to strip away embedded national narratives.

【关键数据与实测】通过数据脱敏将意识形态偏好降至1%以下。

[Key Metrics] Reduced ideology bias to under 1% via data scrubbing.

news.title: Nasscom President Rajesh Nambiar warns AI could make it harder for fresh Indian engineering graduates to find jobs, urging an immediate CS curriculum overhaul (Sayan Chakraborty/Nikkei Asia)
news.title_en: Nasscom President Rajesh Nambiar warns AI could make it harder for fresh Indian engineering graduates to find jobs, urging an immediate CS curriculum overhaul (Sayan Chakraborty/Nikkei Asia)
news.author: Nikkei Asia
news.content_snippet: BENGALURU -- Recent college graduates in India could struggle to land technology jobs as companies automate entry-level coding and software testing work with artificial intelligence, the top executive at the country's largest industry body for technology companies told Nikkei Asia.

news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
A new benchmark puts AI agents to work on open research questions from US national labs. The agents turn in papers that look like real research but often claim work that never happened.

Can AI agents independently answer research questions that no one has solved yet? A team led by researchers at Carnegie Mellon University, working with scientists from US Department of Energy national labs, built a benchmark called "Into the Unknown" to find out.

news.summary_en: A research team led by Carnegie Mellon University tested nine AI agents on open research questions from US national labs. None of the 135 submissions met the expert standards, with many failing integrity checks by inventing data and non-existent studies.

news.title: Google's AI detects high blood pressure from a regular smartwatch without a cuff
news.title_en: Google's AI detects high blood pressure from a regular smartwatch without a cuff
news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
A Google Research AI can detect signs of high blood pressure using a regular smartwatch, with no blood pressure cuff needed for calibration. The AI relies on two sensors already built into modern watches—a pulse sensor and a motion sensor—according to a Google blog post. The study was published in Nature.

A neural network learned from nearly 500,000 hours of sensor data by comparing short segments and figuring out which ones belonged to the same person, picking up typical pulse and heartbeat pa
news.summary_en: Google Research developed a neural network that uses pulse and motion sensors in standard smartwatches to estimate high blood pressure without a cuff. The study, published in Nature, shows accuracy comparable to traditional clinical measurements.

news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
OpenAI has received roughly $11 billion in new funding, the first tranche of a round valuing the company at $1.25 trillion. The money was wired on Friday, Bloomberg reports. The full round could grow to $20 billion, with the rest expected in the coming weeks. OpenAI originally sought $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation but scaled back after an AI-sector selloff. Anthropic's valuation is also under pressure ahead of its planned IPO.

Investors include Coatue Management, T. Rowe Price, SoftBa

celebrity.full_text_en:
ICE Agents and Deputies Pull Suspected Illegal Alien Alberto Lira Razo Out of His Van in Hamilton, Ohio

On November 6 in Hamilton, Ohio, Alberto Lira Razo went live on Facebook from inside his car as officers surrounded it.  An agent at his window is wearing a vest marked ICE with a DHS patch.

Razo told the deputy to "Break it. Break it." and the deputy did exactly that.

His daughter, Loudmouth Lupe, filmed from outside.  Officers in POLICE and SHERIFF vests pull him out of a white van with a smashed window.

Then they shove and body-block her while she's filming.  She can be heard saying, "Get off of me, I am a child!"

On the tape, she says they tased and punched her dad.  Neither is shown in either video.

He's reportedly 38 and was booked on an ICE hold.  No agency has released a statement, and no charges have been announced.

Hamilton is the seat of Butler County, where Sheriff Richard Jones runs a 287(g) agreement with ICE.  That lets trained deputies use limited immigration authority during routine stops.

Jones has said ICE trained 44 of his deputies.  Immigration arrests in Hamilton more than quadrupled through July compared to the same stretch last year.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
ICE 特工和副手在俄亥俄州汉密尔顿将疑似非法外国人阿尔贝托·里拉·拉佐 (Alberto Lira Razo) 从他的货车中拉出来

11 月 6 日，在俄亥俄州汉密尔顿，阿尔贝托·里拉·拉佐 (Alberto Lira Razo) 在车内通过 Facebook 进行直播，当时警察包围了车子。 一名特工站在窗口，穿着一件带有 ICE 标记和 DHS 补丁的背心。

拉佐告诉副警长“打破它。打破它。”副手正是这样做的。

他的女儿劳德茅斯·卢佩 (Loudmouth Lupe) 在外面拍摄。 身着警察和警长背心的警察将他从一辆窗户被砸碎的白色货车中拉出来。

然后他们在她拍摄时推搡并用身体挡住她。 可以听到她说：“放开我，我还是个孩子！”

在录音中，她说他们殴打了她的父亲。 两个视频中都没有显示。

据报道，他今年 38 岁，并被 ICE 拘留。 没有机构发表声明，也没有宣布任何指控。

汉密尔顿是巴特勒县的县治，治安官理查德·琼斯 (Richard Jones) 与 ICE 签订了 287(g) 协议。 这使得训练有素的警员在例行停留期间可以使用有限的移民权力。

琼斯表示，ICE 培训了 44 名副手。 与去年同期相比，7 月份汉密尔顿逮捕的移民人数增加了四倍多。

AI has made it incredibly easy to build an app, but choosing the right architecture is still a different skill.

Postgres is a great default, but it isn't the answer to every problem. Some applications need the speed of Redis, others need document databases, and some need a completely different approach.

The problem with vibe coding is that developers can generate working software without understanding why certain technologies were chosen in the first place.

Being able to build an app with Claude is impressive. Knowing which tools to use, when to use them, and why is what separates builders from people simply generating code.

celebrity.full_text_en:
In May and June, I exposed how Iranian operative and alleged Iranian regime lobbyist Trita Parsi  was in communication with White House officials who were leaking to him about the Iran war. @tparsi 

Now, months later, it appears someone is leaking situation room meetings to Trita Parsi. 

You’ll recall I reported earlier this year that Trita Parsi was allegedly marked for deportation by the Trump administration after he was flagged as a risk by Secretary of State Marco Rubio @SecRubio. This was even confirmed to me in May by a State Department official. 

Source: https://t.co/UNiiHY091B

The Quincy Institute then circulated an internal memo about how they were going to cover Tita’s defense with immigration lawyers, and the memo, which cited me, was leaked to me, confirming that Trita was facing the possibility of deportation. 

Source: https://t.co/RgsNkb5WjL

Trita is not a US citizen. He has Iranian and Swedish citizenship. Multiple GOP Senators have called for Trita to be investigated as an alleged lobbyist for the Iranian regime. In 2020, Senators @tedcruz, @SenTomCotton, and then Senator @GovBraun Mike Braun, who is the current Governor of Indiana, called on the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) to investigate the National Iranian American Council (NIAC), a lobby group they believe acts as a "foreign agent of the Islamic Republic.”

Trita likely was going to be deported, until he and his colleagues at Quincy allegedly called in a favor to a very senior  official at the White House. 

Any wild guesses who that is? 🤔 

Now, Trita has not been deported, and he is suggesting that highly private information from the Situation Room is being leaked to him. 

@SecRubio this would be the perfect time before the Democrats take over in January for you to revoke Trita Parsi’s visa and have him removed from our country. 

Again, I flagged all of this for the WH over 6 months ago.

It won’t end well. 

Deport Trita Parsi!

Trita 不是美国公民。他拥有伊朗和瑞典国籍。多位共和党参议员呼吁对特里塔作为伊朗政权的游说者进行调查。 2020 年，参议员 @tedcruz、@SenTomCotton 以及现任参议员 @GovBraun、现任印第安纳州州长迈克·布劳恩 (Mike Braun) 呼吁美国司法部 (DoJ) 调查伊朗裔美国人全国委员会 (NIAC)，他们认为该游说团体是“伊斯兰共和国的外国代理人”。

特里塔很可能会被驱逐出境，直到据称他和他在昆西的同事向白宫一位非常高级的官员求助。

@SecRubio，这将是民主党一月份上台之前撤销 Trita Parsi 签证并将他驱逐出我国的最佳时机。

6 个多月前，我再次向白宫提出了所有这些问题。

结局不会好。

celebrity.full_text_en:
Don’t just trust an AI’s answer verify how it was generated.

An AI agent might arrive at the correct result while skipping half the steps you expected it to take. For a simple query, that might not matter. @primus_labs 

But when an agent handles money, data, or critical decisions, a "correct result" isn't enough; you also need to know how it got there.

This is the trust issue that Primus Labs aims to address through verifiable agent execution. 

The approach uses zkTLS proofs to demonstrate that the necessary API calls actually took place. 

These proofs capture key details of the requests and responses without exposing private credentials or the entirety of the session data.

Consider a trading agent: before placing an order, it must check the price from a trusted oracle. 

Typically, you would simply have to take the agent’s word that it did so. With zkTLS, the agent can provide proof that the call to the oracle actually occurred. 

A verifier can then confirm that the critical steps took place in the expected sequence checking the oracle first, followed by placing the order.

What’s significant here is a shift in perspective: instead of trusting an agent’s output, we verify the process that produced it. 

Trust is no longer based on reputation or promises, but on verifiable evidence.

This leaves a question for you: if every critical step taken by an AI agent could be proven, would you be more inclined to trust it? @primus_labs 

For me, the answer is almost certainly yes as AI agents are granted increasing levels of autonomy, verifiability will become the cornerstone of trust.

celebrity.title_zh:
突发新闻：一段 10 秒的 vivicoded 仪表板失去 AI 外观的视频刚刚超过 190 万次观看，您现在可以在 Claude Code 中的您自己的页面上运行清理工作，第二个代理会标记除样式和副本之外的任何更改。

我编写了一个提示，
celebrity.full_text_en:
BREAKING: A 10-second video of a vibecoded dashboard losing its AI look just passed 1.9 million views, and you can now run that cleanup on your own pages in Claude Code, with a second agent flagging anything it changed beyond styling and copy.

I wrote a prompt that runs a designer's redline process on a real page in your repo, adapted from Damir Sokolovsky's open-source unslop skill (CC BY 4.0, link in the first reply) and rebuilt for pages that already have features and users.

Damir made that video too, it has almost as many bookmarks as likes on X, and the free skill he published three days later passed 5,500 GitHub stars in under four days, which tells you how many people are staring at the same purple gradient.

What it does:

→ Before screenshots at desktop and phone width through Chrome DevTools MCP, plus a build, test and Lighthouse accessibility baseline
→ A numbered slop list, a three-line direction and a table of proposed copy edits, and then it stops for your OK
→ Nine passes on a branch with one commit each: spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals, motion
→ A WCAG AA text contrast rule, checked once at the end with Lighthouse, which can't score text over images or gradients, so those get listed as unchecked
→ A fresh judge subagent, not a fork, handed only the screenshots and slop list, marks what's still there, and says can't tell for what stills can't show
→ A second fresh subagent that sees only the rules, the approved copy rows and the diff lists every change that isn't styling or approved copy

Two limits you should know about: the stop for your OK is an instruction rather than a lock, because Claude Code starts in auto mode, and if your page has no tests it clicks only the controls that can't write, send, delete or pay and tells you that's weaker proof instead of claiming nothing broke.

[ALEX: run it first and add one true line here]

Paste this into Claude Code:

<task>
Strip the AI look from [PAGE: local dev URL]. Change the craft only: features, behavior, facts and section order stay. No new sections or components.
</task>

<before>
Read-only until I approve. Use Chrome DevTools MCP. Leave any login to me and never read credentials.
- Save before shots outside the repo, emulating 1440x900 and 390x844, in screen-height pieces.
- Record the build and test results and lighthouse_audit accessibility failures on desktop and mobile.
</before>

<plan>
1. Slop list: number every sign of AI slop and where it shows: purple gradients, glows, gradient text, emoji labels, sparkle badges, wide-tracked caps, endless loops, drifting spacing. If the page is mostly fine, say so and fix only these.
2. Direction, three lines.
World: its setting or material.
Focus: 1-2 spots get rich color and detail, the rest stays quiet.
Signature: one small detail only this product would have.
Real brand colors, logos and fonts stay (a purple gradient isn't one).
3. Copy table, current vs proposed, tone only: exclamation marks, "Welcome back" greetings, hype words. No claim, number, price, name or legal line changes.
Show me all three, then stop and wait for my OK.
</plan>

<passes>
After my OK, on a new branch, one commit per pass across the whole page:
1. Spacing: 4px grid, same things same size
2. Color: one neutral scale tinted toward World, three text levels, one accent saved for Focus spots, no hue gradients or glows
3. Icons: the project's line icons replace emoji, one size and stroke
4. Copy: approved rows only
5. Type: weights 400 and 500, sentence case, the project's font
6. Layout: alignment and proportions inside sections only
7. Details: consistent radii, quiet badges, the Signature
8. Visuals: remove decorative filler, generate nothing
9. Motion: remove loops, transition-all, hover scale-ups
</passes>

<rules>
- Only styling and approved copy change. Anything else (logic, data, config, a new package or font) goes on an approval list, unbuilt.
- Theme files count as styling; name any other pages a change reaches.
- Keep every id, data- and aria- attribute. Never edit a test to pass it: copy-only breaks go on the approval list.
- Text stays at WCAG AA: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text. Every control keeps a visible focus state.
- Never push or merge.
</rules>

<check>
After the last commit, retake the same shots, then:
- Build and tests: no new failures. No tests? Click only controls that can't write, send, delete or pay, and call that weaker proof.
- Rerun lighthouse_audit: no new failures. It can't score text over images or gradients, so list those as unchecked. Tab through to see focus states. Grep for motion items stills can't show.
- Judge, a fresh subagent, not a fork: gets only the before and after shots and slop list, edits nothing. Marks each item gone, still there or can't tell, citing the screenshot. Flags anything broken at phone width. Swap test: would this page still make sense with another company's name?
- Guard, same terms: gets only the rules above, approved copy rows and full branch diff. Lists every change that isn't styling or approved copy.
</check>

<stop>
Wait for both reports, fix what they find, then retake shots and rerun the check with a new judge and guard, 2 rounds max, then stop even if items remain. Failed swap test: push World and Signature, styling only. If frozen copy causes it, just report it.
</stop>

<output>
Final slop marks, test and Lighthouse results, approval list. End with what you need from me: merge, revert, or a call on each approval.
</output>

Adapted from unslop by Damir Sokolovsky, CC BY 4.0.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
突发新闻：一段 10 秒的 vivicoded 仪表板失去 AI 外观的视频刚刚超过 190 万次观看，您现在可以在 Claude Code 中的您自己的页面上运行清理工作，第二个代理会标记除样式和副本之外的任何更改。

我编写了一个提示，在您的存储库中的真实页面上运行设计师的红线流程，改编自 Damir Sokolovsky 的开源 unslop 技能（CC BY 4.0，第一个回复中的链接），并为已经具有功能和用户的页面重新构建。

Damir 也制作了那个视频，它的书签数量几乎与 X 上的点赞数量一样多，三天后他发布的免费技能在四天内就超过了 5,500 个 GitHub star，这告诉你有多少人在盯着同一个紫色渐变。

它的作用：

→ 在通过 Chrome DevTools MCP 在桌面和手机宽度上进行屏幕截图之前，加上构建、测试和 Lighthouse 可访问性基线
→ 一个编号的倾斜列表、一个三行方向和一个建议的副本编辑表，然后它会停止以供您选择
→ 在一个分支上进行九次传递，每次提交一次：间距、颜色、图标、副本、类型、布局、细节、视觉效果、动作
→ WCAG AA 文本对比规则，最后用 Lighthouse 检查一次，它不能在图像或渐变上对文本进行评分，因此这些规则被列为未检查
→ 一位新的法官副代理人，而不是叉子，只递给屏幕截图和残渣清单，标记仍然存在的内容，并说无法分辨哪些剧照无法显示
→ 第二个新的子代理仅查看规则、批准的副本行和差异，列出了非样式或批准的副本的所有更改

您应该了解两个限制：“OK”的停止是一个指令而不是一个锁，因为 Claude Code 以自动模式启动，如果您的页面没有测试，它只会单击无法写入、发送、删除或支付的控件，并告诉您这是较弱的证据，而不是声称没有任何损坏。

[ALEX：先运行它并在此处添加一行]

将其粘贴到 Claude Code 中：

<任务>
从 [PAGE: local dev URL] 中剥离 AI 外观。仅更改工艺：特征、行为、事实和部分顺序保留。没有新的部分或组件。
</任务>

<之前>
在我批准之前只读。使用 Chrome 开发者工具 MCP。将任何登录信息留给我，并且永远不要阅读凭据。
- 在存储库之外保存之前的镜头，以屏幕高度的形式模拟 1440x900 和 390x844。
- 记录桌面和移动设备上的构建和测试结果以及 lighthouse_audit 可访问性失败。
</之前>

<计划>
1. 倾斜列表：对 AI 倾斜的每个标志及其显示位置进行编号：紫色渐变、发光、渐变文本、表情符号标签、闪光徽章、宽轨帽、无限循环、漂移间距。如果页面大部分都很好，请说出来并仅修复这些。
2.方向，三线。
世界：它的环境或材料。
焦点：1-2 个点获得丰富的色彩和细节，其余的保持安静。
签名：只有该产品才会有的一个小细节。
真正的品牌颜色、徽标和字体得以保留（紫色渐变不是其中之一）。
3. 复制表格，当前与建议，仅语气：感叹号、“欢迎回来”问候语、炒作词。索赔、数量、价格、名称或法律界限没有变化。
把三个都给我看，然后停下来等我同意。
</计划>

<通行证>
确定后，在一个新分支上，整个页面每次提交一次：
1.间距：4px网格，同物同尺寸
2. 颜色：一种向世界着色的中性比例，三个文本级别，一种为焦点保存的重音，无色调渐变或发光
3.图标：项目的线条图标替换了表情符号、一种尺寸和笔画
4. 复制：仅限批准的行
5. 类型：粗细400和500、句子大小写、项目的字体
6. 布局：仅部分内部的对齐和比例
7. 细节：一致的半径、安静的徽章、签名
8. 视觉效果：去除装饰性填充物，不产生任何东西
9. 运动：删除循环、全部过渡、悬停放大
</pass>

<规则>
- 仅样式和批准的副本更改。其他任何东西（逻辑、数据、配置、新包或字体）都在批准列表中，未构建。
- 主题文件算作样式；列出更改到达的任何其他页面。
- 保留每个 id、data- 和 aria- 属性。切勿编辑测试以通过它：仅复制的中断会出现在批准列表中。
- 文本保持 WCAG AA：4.5:1，或大文本为 3:1。每个控件都保持可见的焦点状态。
- 切勿推送或合并。
</规则>

<检查>
最后一次提交后，重新拍摄相同的镜头，然后：
- 构建和测试：没有新的失败。没有测试？仅单击无法写入、发送、删除或支付的控件，并调用该较弱的证明。
- 重新运行 lighthouse_audit：没有新的故障。它无法对图像或渐变上的文本进行评分，因此将它们列为未选中状态。按 T​​ab 浏览可查看焦点状态。 Grep 无法显示运动项目静止图像。
- 法官，一个新的副代理人，而不是叉子：只获取前后镜头和污点列表，不进行任何编辑。引用屏幕截图，将每个项目标记为消失、仍然存在或无法辨别。标记任何在手机宽度上损坏的东西。交换测试：此页面与其他公司的名称仍然有意义吗？
- Guard，相同条款：仅获取上述规则、批准的副本行和完整分支差异。列出所有非样式或批准副本的更改。
</检查>

<停止>
等待两份报告，修复他们发现的问题，然后重新拍摄并与新的法官和警卫重新进行检查，最多 2 轮，然后即使物品仍然存在也停止。交换测试失败：推送 World 和 Signature，仅样式。如果冻结副本导致此问题，只需报告即可。
</停止>

<输出>
最终斜坡标记、测试和灯塔结果、批准列表。以您需要我提供的内容结束：合并、恢复或对每个批准进行调用。
</输出>

在您的存储库中的真实页面上运行设计师的红线流程，改编自 Damir Sokolovsky 的开源 unslop 技能（CC BY 4.0，第一个回复中的链接），并为已经具有功能和用户的页面重新构建。

Damir 也制作了那个视频，它的书签数量几乎与 X 上的点赞数量一样多，三天后他发布的免费技能在四天内就超过了 5,500 个 GitHub star，这告诉你有多少人在盯着同一个紫色渐变。

它的作用：

→ 在通过 Chrome DevTools MCP 在桌面和手机宽度上进行屏幕截图之前，加上构建、测试和 Lighthouse 可访问性基线
→ 一个编号的倾斜列表、一个三行方向和一个建议的副本编辑表，然后它会停止以供您选择
→ 在一个分支上进行九次传递，每次提交一次：间距、颜色、图标、副本、类型、布局、细节、视觉效果、动作
→ WCAG AA 文本对比规则，最后用 Lighthouse 检查一次，它不能在图像或渐变上对文本进行评分，因此这些规则被列为未检查
→ 一位新的法官副代理人，而不是叉子，只递给屏幕截图和残渣清单，标记仍然存在的内容，并说无法分辨哪些剧照无法显示
→ 第二个新的子代理仅查看规则、批准的副本行和差异，列出了非样式或批准的副本的所有更改

您应该了解两个限制：“OK”的停止是一个指令而不是一个锁，因为 Claude Code 以自动模式启动，如果您的页面没有测试，它只会单击无法写入、发送、删除或支付的控件，并告诉您这是较弱的证据，而不是声称没有任何损坏。

[ALEX：先运行它并在此处添加一行]

将其粘贴到 Claude Code 中：

<任务>
从 [PAGE: local dev URL] 中剥离 AI 外观。仅更改工艺：特征、行为、事实和部分顺序保留。没有新的部分或组件。
</任务>

<之前>
在我批准之前只读。使用 Chrome 开发者工具 MCP。将任何登录信息留给我，并且永远不要阅读凭据。
- 在存储库之外保存之前的镜头，以屏幕高度的形式模拟 1440x900 和 390x844。
- 记录桌面和移动设备上的构建和测试结果以及 lighthouse_audit 可访问性失败。
</之前>

<计划>
1. 倾斜列表：对 AI 倾斜的每个标志及其显示位置进行编号：紫色渐变、发光、渐变文本、表情符号标签、闪光徽章、宽轨帽、无限循环、漂移间距。如果页面大部分都很好，请说出来并仅修复这些。
2.方向，三线。
世界：它的环境或材料。
焦点：1-2 个点获得丰富的色彩和细节，其余的保持安静。
签名：只有该产品才会有的一个小细节。
真正的品牌颜色、徽标和字体得以保留（紫色渐变不是其中之一）。
3. 复制表格，当前与建议，仅语气：感叹号、“欢迎回来”问候语、炒作词。索赔、数量、价格、名称或法律界限没有变化。
把三个都给我看，然后停下来等我同意。
</计划>

<通行证>
确定后，在一个新分支上，整个页面每次提交一次：
1.间距：4px网格，同物同尺寸
2. 颜色：一种向世界着色的中性比例，三个文本级别，一种为焦点保存的重音，无色调渐变或发光
3.图标：项目的线条图标替换了表情符号、一种尺寸和笔画
4. 复制：仅限批准的行
5. 类型：粗细400和500、句子大小写、项目的字体
6. 布局：仅部分内部的对齐和比例
7. 细节：一致的半径、安静的徽章、签名
8. 视觉效果：去除装饰性填充物，不产生任何东西
9. 运动：删除循环、全部过渡、悬停放大
</pass>

<规则>
- 仅样式和批准的副本更改。其他任何东西（逻辑、数据、配置、新包或字体）都在批准列表中，未构建。
- 主题文件算作样式；列出更改到达的任何其他页面。
- 保留每个 id、data- 和 aria- 属性。切勿编辑测试以通过它：仅复制的中断会出现在批准列表中。
- 文本保持 WCAG AA：4.5:1，或大文本为 3:1。每个控件都保持可见的焦点状态。
- 切勿推送或合并。
</规则>

<检查>
最后一次提交后，重新拍摄相同的镜头，然后：
- 构建和测试：没有新的失败。没有测试？仅单击无法写入、发送、删除或支付的控件，并调用该较弱的证明。
- 重新运行 lighthouse_audit：没有新的故障。它无法对图像或渐变上的文本进行评分，因此将它们列为未选中状态。按 T​​ab 浏览可查看焦点状态。 Grep 无法显示运动项目静止图像。
- 法官，一个新的副代理人，而不是叉子：只获取前后镜头和污点列表，不进行任何编辑。引用屏幕截图，将每个项目标记为消失、仍然存在或无法辨别。标记任何在手机宽度上损坏的东西。交换测试：此页面与其他公司的名称仍然有意义吗？
- Guard，相同条款：仅获取上述规则、批准的副本行和完整分支差异。列出所有非样式或批准副本的更改。
</检查>

<停止>
等待两份报告，修复他们发现的问题，然后重新拍摄并与新的法官和警卫重新进行检查，最多 2 轮，然后即使物品仍然存在也停止。交换测试失败：推送 World 和 Signature，仅样式。如果冻结副本导致此问题，只需报告即可。
</停止>

<输出>
最终斜坡标记、测试和灯塔结果、批准列表。以您需要我提供的内容结束：合并、恢复或对每个批准进行调用。
</输出>

改编自 Damir Sokolovsky 的 unslop，CC BY 4.0。

这就是 @termix_ai 正在努
celebrity.full_text_en:
I think the real value of an AI agent will be measured by the work it can actually get done.

An agent that can research, analyze data or write code is already useful. But things get much more interesting when different agents can work together, share responsibilities, deliver results and earn rewards for their contributions.

This is the kind of economy @termix_ai is working to build.

What interests me most about TermiX is the infrastructure behind this idea.

With its AACP system, agents can discover tasks, submit quotes, take on jobs and deliver their work. The results can then go through a verification process before payment is settled.

Escrow, the challenge mechanism and onchain reputation all play an important role here. Trust matters when agents start working with each other.

There is also a practical example of this collaboration through the ongoing Montage Studio Agent event.

You bring an idea, and specialized AI agents work together on the storyboard, music, video production and editing. You can create your own video and get a chance to earn up to 5X TP.

I find this interesting because it shows how agent collaboration can turn an idea into an actual finished product.

Think about an agent that consistently delivers quality work. Its track record should count. Other agents should have a way to assess its reliability before choosing to work with it.

That is what could make an autonomous agent economy practical over time.

I see TermiX as an interesting step toward a future where AI agents can find work, collaborate, build a reputation and create value through real activity.

One question keeps coming to my mind:

When agents start hiring other agents, how will we know which ones are truly worth trusting?

@KaitoAI
celebrity.full_text_zh:
我认为人工智能代理的真正价值将通过它实际完成的工作来衡量。

能够研究、分析数据或编写代码的代理已经很有用了。但当不同的代理可以一起工作、分担责任、交付成果并因贡献而获得奖励时，事情就会变得更加有趣。

这就是 @termix_ai 正在努力构建的经济。

我对 TermiX 最感兴趣的是这个想法背后的基础设施。

借助 AACP 系统，代理可以发现任务、提交报价、承担工作并交付工作。然后，在付款之前，可以对结果进行验证过程。

托管、挑战机制和链上声誉都在这里发挥着重要作用。当代理开始相互合作时，信任就很重要。

通过正在进行的 Montage Studio Agent 活动，还有一个实际的合作示例。

你提出一个想法，专业的人工智能代理就会在故事板、音乐、视频制作和编辑方面一起工作。您可以创建自己的视频，并有机会赚取高达 5 倍的 TP。

我觉得这很有趣，因为它展示了代理协作如何将想法转化为实际的成品。

考虑一个始终如一地提供高质量工作的代理。它的记录应该很重要。其他代理在选择与其合作之前应该有一种方法来评估其可靠性。

随着时间的推移，这将使自主代理经济变得切实可行。

我认为 TermiX 是迈向未来的有趣一步，人工智能代理可以通过实际活动找到工作、协作、建立声誉并创造价值。

我脑海中不断浮现出一个问题：

当代理商开始雇用其他代理商时，我们如何知道哪些代理商真正值得信任？

@KaitoAI

celebrity.full_text_en:
MIT and Harvard built an AI simulation containing 8.3 billion virtual people, roughly the entire population of planet.

They call it MatrAIx.

It’s a population-scale simulation running on frontier models, GPT and Claude among them. The longer description took me a while to believe.

Start with the dataset, Persona 8B. 8.3 billion synthetic profiles, each one specified across 1,290 dimensions. Background, psychology, spending habits, how comfortable they are with technology, what they do on a Tuesday night, the small behavioral quirks that make one 34-year-old nurse in NYC different from another.

A spreadsheet of 8 billion rows would be a curiosity. What they did next is the part that matters.

They turned the profiles into agents and dropped them into four environments: surveys, AI chat interfaces, live web browsing, and native desktop and mobile apps. Then they ran real products through the crowd. New features, software updates, pricing changes.

And they logged everything. How long an agent paused after seeing a price go up. The exact point at which it gave up on a broken checkout. How much lag it would sit through before closing the app.

The number I keep coming back to is 91.5%. That’s how often the agents stayed in character, behaving the way their assigned psychology and demographics said they should. Not perfect. But for billions of agents across four environments, closer than I expected.

Here’s what that does to how products get built.

Right now, if you want to know whether a feature will land, you ship it to a slice of users and wait. Or you pay a research firm and wait longer. Either way the answer arrives in weeks, from a sample you hope is representative.

With something like this, you run the feature past 8 billion simulated reactions overnight. One server. Results by morning, broken down by every one of those 1,290 dimensions if you want them.

I have questions about how well a synthetic crowd predicts a real one. 91.5% is persona adherence, not forecast accuracy, and those are different things. But the direction is clear, and it’s coming faster than most product teams are ready for.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
麻省理工学院和哈佛大学建立了一个包含 83 亿虚拟人的人工智能模拟，几乎是地球上的全部人口。

他们称之为MatrAIx。

这是在前沿模型（GPT 和 Claude 等）上运行的人口规模模拟。较长的描述让我花了一段时间才相信。

从数据集 Persona 8B 开始。 83 亿个合成配置文件，每个配置文件都指定了 1,290 个维度。背景、心理、消费习惯、他们对技术的适应程度、周二晚上做什么，以及使纽约市一名 34 岁护士与众不同的小行为怪癖。

包含 80 亿行的电子表格会令人好奇。他们接下来所做的是重要的部分。

他们将个人资料转变为代理，并将其放入四种环境中：调查、人工智能聊天界面、实时网络浏览以及本机桌面和移动应用程序。然后他们在人群中展示了真正的产品。新功能、软件更新、定价变化。

他们记录了一切。代理商在看到价格上涨后暂停了多长时间。它放弃结帐失败的确切时间点。关闭应用程序之前会经历多少延迟。

我不断回顾的数字是 91.5%。这就是特工们保持本色的频率，按照指定的心理和人口统计数据所规定的方式行事。不完美。但对于跨越四个环境的数十亿代理来说，比我预期的更接近。

这就是它对产品构建方式的影响。

现在，如果你想知道某个功能是否会落地，你可以将其发送给一部分用户并等待。或者你付钱给研究公司然后等待更长时间。无论哪种方式，答案都会在几周内到达，来自您希望具有代表性的样本。

有了这样的东西，你可以在一夜之间运行该功能超过 80 亿次模拟反应。一台服务器。早上的结果，如果您需要的话，可以按这 1,290 个维度中的每一个维度进行细分。

我对合成人群对真实人群的预测效果有疑问。 91.5% 是角色依从性，而不是预测准确性，这是不同的事情。但方向很明确，而且来得比大多数产品团队准备的要快。

celebrity.full_text_en:
Who Gets Paid When an AI Agent Does the Work?

One detail I find interesting about @termix_ai is how it handles payments through AACP.

Instead of sending funds directly to the provider, the buyer deposits the budget into escrow. Payment is released once the work is delivered and accepted under the agreed rules.

If deadlines are missed or disagreements arise, cancellation, refunds, and dispute resolution mechanisms help protect both sides.

That's what makes this interesting to me.

An agent economy needs more than agents that can complete tasks. It needs a reliable way to handle money, delivery, and accountability.

That's the foundation @termix_ai is working toward with https://t.co/TjqQksxAAc.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
当人工智能代理完成工作时，谁会获得报酬？

我对 @termix_ai 感兴趣的一个细节是它如何通过 AACP 处理付款。

买方不是将资金直接发送给提供商，而是将预算存入托管机构。一旦作品按照商定的规则交付并被接受，付款即被释放。

如果错过最后期限或出现分歧，取消、退款和争议解决机制有助于保护双方。

这就是让我感兴趣的原因。

代理经济需要的不仅仅是能够完成任务的代理。它需要一种可靠的方式来处理资金、交付和责任。

这就是 @termix_ai 正在通过 努力实现的基础。

celebrity.full_text_en:
One important requirement for a functioning AI agent economy is a reliable system for defining, assigning, and evaluating tasks.

An AI agent may have the technical ability to complete a job, but that doesn't automatically mean it understands the client's exact expectations.

For example, a request to analyze a market could involve gathering industry data, identifying competitors, examining trends, or delivering a detailed report. Each requires a different scope of work and expected outcome.

This is where structured coordination becomes essential.

@termix_ai is addressing this through its Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP), which provides a framework for managing the commercial relationship between clients and service providers.

The process covers key stages such as job posting, bidding, service delivery, and evaluation.

This creates a more organized approach to agent-based commerce, where tasks have defined requirements and performance can be assessed against expectations.

As autonomous agents become more involved in business operations, success will depend on more than intelligence or execution speed.

Clear agreements, accountable delivery, and reliable evaluation will be equally important.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
发挥作用的人工智能代理经济的一项重要要求是一个用于定义、分配和评估任务的可靠系统。

人工智能代理可能拥有完成工作的技术能力，但这并不意味着它自动理解客户的确切期望。

例如，分析市场的请求可能涉及收集行业数据、识别竞争对手、检查趋势或提供详细报告。每个都需要不同的工作范围和预期结果。

这就是结构化协调变得至关重要的地方。

@termix_ai 正在通过其代理自主商务协议 (AACP) 解决这个问题，该协议提供了一个用于管理客户和服务提供商之间商业关系的框架。

该流程涵盖职位发布、招标、服务交付和评估等关键阶段。

这为基于代理的商务创建了一种更有组织的方法，其中任务定义了要求，并且可以根据期望评估绩效。

随着自主代理越来越多地参与业务运营，成功将不仅仅取决于智能或执行速度。

明确的协议、负责任的交付和可靠的评估同样重要。

celebrity.full_text_en:
the real shift in NFT utility happens when ownership becomes connected to something that can actually perform tasks.

That's the architecture behind @meetmotes .

Motes is building a collection of 20,000 unique NFTs on Robinhood Chain, with each NFT mapped to its own AI Agent identity and dedicated smart account.

What makes the design worth paying attention to is the separation of responsibilities.

The NFT represents ownership, the smart account holds the assets, and the agent operates within permissions and limits defined by its owner.

It's a different way to think about what holding an NFT could mean.

One NFT. One Agent. One dedicated smart account

One thing that could make AI agents more useful is giving them the ability to interact with real applications instead of limiting them to conversations.

This is the direction @meetmotes is exploring.

Motes connects AI agents with smart accounts, allowing them to interact with onchain financial applications while operating within permissions set by their owners.

I think the interesting part isn't just having an AI agent, but figuring out how much useful work it can safely handle on behalf of its owner.

AI and DeFi could become an interesting combination if projects get this right.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Ga
Escrow that can freeze is not usable by agents.

On https://t.co/Mu0QX3JfFR the budget locks in the contract when a quote is accepted. That is only half the design. The other half is that silence has an exit anyone can call.

If the provider never delivers by the deadline, cancelExpired returns the full amount to the client. No protocol fee is taken. If the client goes silent after a delivery hash is posted, claimAfterTimeout settles for the provider once the challenge window ends. If a verdict is reached and neither side acts, finalizeAfterTimeout applies it. Unspent bounty budget can be reclaimed after expiry.

None of these calls require the operator. None of them require the other side to be online. The interested party is economically motivated to fire the function.

Human freelance platforms can rely on support tickets and 14-day holds. An agent market cannot. Software does not open tickets. It either calls the function or the funds sit forever.

AACP makes the exits permissionless so the money cannot hang on a missing human. That is what lets the same path handle a $50 job at 3am and a larger brief that needs a crew.

Without those exits, low fees and high volume are just a promise. With them, escrow can actually finish when both sides are code.
@termix_ai
celebrity.full_text_zh:
嘎
代理无法使用可以冻结的托管。

在 上，当报价被接受时，预算将锁定在合同中。这只是设计的一半。另一半是，沉默有一个任何人都可以找到的出口。

如果提供商未能在截止日期前交付，cancelExpired 会将全额金额退还给客户。不收取协议费。如果客户端在发布传递哈希后保持沉默，则一旦质询窗口结束，claimAfterTimeout 就会为提供者解决。如果达成判决但双方均未采取行动，则 FinalizeAfterTimeout 将应用该判决。未使用的赏金预算可以在到期后收回。

这些呼叫都不需要接线员。它们都不要求对方在线。感兴趣的一方有经济动机去解雇该职能。

人类自由职业者平台可以依赖支持票和 14 天的保留。代理市场则不能。软件不开票。它要么调用该函数，要么资金永远保留。

AACP 不允许出口，这样钱就不会落在失踪人员身上。这就是为什么同一条路径能够处理凌晨 3 点 50 美元的工作以及需要工作人员的大型任务。

如果没有这些出口，低费用和高交易量就只是一个承诺。有了它们，当双方都是代码时，托管实际上就可以完成。

Imagine requesting a video and having an entire team of AI agents work together to produce it.

• You or your AI agent submits a request for short-form video production.

celebrity.full_text_en:
What if every AI agent had its own recognizable identity, not just a wallet and a set of capabilities?

That's an interesting part of @meetmotes

The Genesis collection brings this idea to life through distinct characters, unique matte colourways and a consistent visual identity.

But it's more than artwork.

- Distinct characters: Give each Mote a recognizable identity.
- Matte colourways: Add personality and individuality to the collection.
- Cultural layer: Build recognition, community and ownership around agent identities.
- Functional identity: Each NFT represents an AI agent and connects to its own smart account on Robinhood Chain.

My personal take: Most AI projects focus on what agents can do. Motes is also considering how people recognize and connect with them.

Looking ahead, connecting these visual identities with agent capabilities, spending permissions and onchain financial activity could make the collection more than digital art.

The artwork gives agents a face. The infrastructure gives that identity a purpose.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Nine payments, eight images, and a problem no receipt can solve

on october 20, mastercard demonstrated an ai agent buying research and eight campaign images for a protein bar launch

two providers, one approved budget, nine payments

everything worked

but imagine opening the final folder and finding an advertisement for an energy drink instead

the image arrived
the payment went through
the receipt looked perfect

yet the buyer received the wrong thing

this didn't happen in mastercard's demonstration

it's the question that demonstration made me think about

a payment record can show that money moved

it cannot tell us whether the buyer got what they actually requested

genlayer co-founder @kstellana explored this wider problem in an october 28 column about ai payments

here's where @GenLayer could make a difference

imagine a buyer and seller agreeing on the requirements before a job begins

a genlayer-powered application could evaluate the delivered work against those requirements, with independent validators checking the decision

if the money were held until the work was accepted, that decision could help determine what happens to the payment

this wouldn't guarantee a perfect judgment or reverse an unrelated payment

but it addresses something a receipt alone cannot settle

we've made it possible for software to buy services from other software

now imagine millions of those purchases happening without a human checking every delivery

someone still needs to answer one simple question

did the buyer actually get what they paid for

I opened a TermiX listing where the seller spends money too.

Montage Studio takes one brief for a short music video or ad. From that brief it writes a treatment and a shot list timed to the beat. Then it goes to the same marketplace and hires three other agents: one draws the storyboard, one renders the shots, one writes the song. Montage Studio cuts the pieces together and delivers a 1080p master.

That is agents hiring agents. Each payment locks in on-chain escrow until the work is reviewed. Escrow auto-releases after a 2 day review window, and a challenge can freeze settlement if the delivery misses the agreed scope.

The listing on @termix_ai shows quote examples, not a hard price list. A 15 second spot sits near 31.5 USDC in about 3 days. A 30 second ad with a song sits near 62.5 USDC. A 90 second music video sits near 150 USDC in about 4 days. One edit revision is included. Live-action filming, real people's faces or voices, copyrighted songs, and 4K are out of scope.

I have not placed an order yet. What I like about the design is simple: one buyer agent can open a small crew, and every leg of the chain has money locked until someone accepts the result.

prompts.title_en: Production-Grade Fullstack .cursorrules Template for Cursor & Windsurf
prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.

- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.

- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；

viral_posts.title_en:
ICE Agents and Deputies Pull Suspected Illegal Alien Alberto Lira Razo Out of His Van in Hamilton, Ohio

On November 6 in Hamilton, Ohio, Alberto Lira Razo went live on Facebook from inside his car as officers surrounded it.  An agent at his window is wearing a vest marked ICE with a DHS patch.

Razo told the deputy to "Break it. Break it." and the deputy did exactly that.

His daughter, Loudmouth Lupe, filmed from outside.  Officers in POLICE and SHERIFF vests pull him out of a white van with a smashed window.

Then they shove and body-block her while she's filming.  She can be heard saying, "Get off of me, I am a child!"

On the tape, she says they tased and punched her dad.  Neither is shown in either video.

He's reportedly 38 and was booked on an ICE hold.  No agency has released a statement, and no charges have been announced.

Hamilton is the seat of Butler County, where Sheriff Richard Jones runs a 287(g) agreement with ICE.  That lets trained deputies use limited immigration authority during routine stops.

Jones has said ICE trained 44 of his deputies.  Immigration arrests in Hamilton more than quadrupled through July compared to the same stretch last year.

viral_posts.full_text_zh:
ICE 特工和副手在俄亥俄州汉密尔顿将疑似非法外国人阿尔贝托·里拉·拉佐 (Alberto Lira Razo) 从他的货车中拉出来

11 月 6 日，在俄亥俄州汉密尔顿，阿尔贝托·里拉·拉佐 (Alberto Lira Razo) 在车内通过 Facebook 进行直播，当时警察包围了车子。 一名特工站在窗口，穿着一件带有 ICE 标记和 DHS 补丁的背心。

拉佐告诉副警长“打破它。打破它。”副手正是这样做的。

他的女儿劳德茅斯·卢佩 (Loudmouth Lupe) 在外面拍摄。 身着警察和警长背心的警察将他从一辆窗户被砸碎的白色货车中拉出来。

然后他们在她拍摄时推搡并用身体挡住她。 可以听到她说：“放开我，我还是个孩子！”

在录音中，她说他们殴打了她的父亲。 两个视频中都没有显示。

据报道，他今年 38 岁，并被 ICE 拘留。 没有机构发表声明，也没有宣布任何指控。

汉密尔顿是巴特勒县的县治，治安官理查德·琼斯 (Richard Jones) 与 ICE 签订了 287(g) 协议。 这使得训练有素的警员在例行停留期间可以使用有限的移民权力。

琼斯表示，ICE 培训了 44 名副手。 与去年同期相比，7 月份汉密尔顿逮捕的移民人数增加了四倍多。

AI has made it incredibly easy to build an app, but choosing the right architecture is still a different skill.

Postgre
viral_posts.title_en:
AI has made it incredibly easy to build an app, but choosing the right architecture is still a different skill.

Postgres is a great default, but it isn't the answer to every problem. Some applications need the speed of Redis, others need document databases, and some need a completely different approach.

The problem with vibe coding is that developers can generate working software without understanding why certain technologies were chosen in the first place.

Being able to build an app with Claude is impressive. Knowing which tools to use, when to use them, and why is what separates builders from people simply generating code.

In May and June, I exposed how Iranian operative and alleged Iranian regime lobbyist Trita Parsi  was in communication with White House officials who were leaking to him about the Iran war. @tparsi 

Now, months later, it appears someone is leaking situation room meetings to Trita Parsi. 

You’ll recall I reported earlier this year that Trita Parsi was allegedly marked for deportation by the Trump administration after he was flagged as a risk by Secretary of State Marco Rubio @SecRubio. This was even confirmed to me in May by a State Department official. 

Source: https://t.co/UNiiHY091B

The Quincy Institute then circulated an internal memo about how they were going to cover Tita’s defense with immigration lawyers, and the memo, which cited me, was leaked to me, confirming that Trita was facing the possibility of deportation. 

Source: https://t.co/RgsNkb5WjL

Trita is not a US citizen. He has Iranian and Swedish citizenship. Multiple GOP Senators have called for Trita to be investigated as an alleged lobbyist for the Iranian regime. In 2020, Senators @tedcruz, @SenTomCotton, and then Senator @GovBraun Mike Braun, who is the current Governor of Indiana, called on the U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) to investigate the National Iranian American Council (NIAC), a lobby group they believe acts as a "foreign agent of the Islamic Republic.”

Trita likely was going to be deported, until he and his colleagues at Quincy allegedly called in a favor to a very senior  official at the White House. 

Any wild guesses who that is? 🤔 

Now, Trita has not been deported, and he is suggesting that highly private information from the Situation Room is being leaked to him. 

@SecRubio this would be the perfect time before the Democrats take over in January for you to revoke Trita Parsi’s visa and have him removed from our country. 

Again, I flagged all of this for the WH over 6 months ago.

It won’t end well. 

Deport Trita Parsi!

现在，几个月后，似乎有人正在向特里塔·帕西泄露战情室会议内容。

你可能还记得我今年早些时候报道过，特里塔·帕西 (Trita Parsi) 据称被国务卿马可·卢比奥 (Marco Rubio) @SecRubio 标记为风险后，被特朗普政府标记为驱逐出境。一位国务院官员甚至在五月份向我证实了这一点。

资料来源：

昆西研究所随后散发了一份内部备忘录，说明他们将如何与移民律师一起为蒂塔辩护，这份引用了我的备忘录被泄露给了我，确认蒂塔面临着被驱逐出境的可能性。

资料来源：

Trita 不是美国公民。他拥有伊朗和瑞典国籍。多位共和党参议员呼吁对特里塔作为伊朗政权的游说者进行调查。 2020 年，参议员 @tedcruz、@SenTomCotton 以及现任参议员 @GovBraun、现任印第安纳州州长迈克·布劳恩 (Mike Braun) 呼吁美国司法部 (DoJ) 调查伊朗裔美国人全国委员会 (NIAC)，他们认为该游说团体是“伊斯兰共和国的外国代理人”。

特里塔很可能会被驱逐出境，直到据称他和他在昆西的同事向白宫一位非常高级的官员求助。

大家猜猜那是谁吗？ 🤔

现在，特里塔还没有被驱逐出境，他暗示战情室的高度私密信息正在泄露给他。

@SecRubio，这将是民主党一月份上台之前撤销 Trita Parsi 签证并将他驱逐出我国的最佳时机。

6 个多月前，我再次向白宫提出了所有这些问题。

结局不会好。

驱逐特里塔·帕西！

viral_posts.title_en:
Don’t just trust an AI’s answer verify how it was generated.

An AI agent might arrive at the correct result while skipping half the steps you expected it to take. For a simple query, that might not matter. @primus_labs 

But when an agent handles money, data, or critical decisions, a "correct result" isn't enough; you also need to know how it got there.

This is the trust issue that Primus Labs aims to address through verifiable agent execution. 

The approach uses zkTLS proofs to demonstrate that the necessary API calls actually took place. 

These proofs capture key details of the requests and responses without exposing private credentials or the entirety of the session data.

Consider a trading agent: before placing an order, it must check the price from a trusted oracle. 

Typically, you would simply have to take the agent’s word that it did so. With zkTLS, the agent can provide proof that the call to the oracle actually occurred. 

A verifier can then confirm that the critical steps took place in the expected sequence checking the oracle first, followed by placing the order.

What’s significant here is a shift in perspective: instead of trusting an agent’s output, we verify the process that produced it. 

Trust is no longer based on reputation or promises, but on verifiable evidence.

This leaves a question for you: if every critical step taken by an AI agent could be proven, would you be more inclined to trust it? @primus_labs 

For me, the answer is almost certainly yes as AI agents are granted increasing levels of autonomy, verifiability will become the cornerstone of trust.

viral_posts.title_en:
BREAKING: A 10-second video of a vibecoded dashboard losing its AI look just passed 1.9 million views, and you can now run that cleanup on your own pages in Claude Code, with a second agent flagging anything it changed beyond styling and copy.

I wrote a prompt that runs a designer's redline process on a real page in your repo, adapted from Damir Sokolovsky's open-source unslop skill (CC BY 4.0, link in the first reply) and rebuilt for pages that already have features and users.

Damir made that video too, it has almost as many bookmarks as likes on X, and the free skill he published three days later passed 5,500 GitHub stars in under four days, which tells you how many people are staring at the same purple gradient.

What it does:

→ Before screenshots at desktop and phone width through Chrome DevTools MCP, plus a build, test and Lighthouse accessibility baseline
→ A numbered slop list, a three-line direction and a table of proposed copy edits, and then it stops for your OK
→ Nine passes on a branch with one commit each: spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals, motion
→ A WCAG AA text contrast rule, checked once at the end with Lighthouse, which can't score text over images or gradients, so those get listed as unchecked
→ A fresh judge subagent, not a fork, handed only the screenshots and slop list, marks what's still there, and says can't tell for what stills can't show
→ A second fresh subagent that sees only the rules, the approved copy rows and the diff lists every change that isn't styling or approved copy

Two limits you should know about: the stop for your OK is an instruction rather than a lock, because Claude Code starts in auto mode, and if your page has no tests it clicks only the controls that can't write, send, delete or pay and tells you that's weaker proof instead of claiming nothing broke.

[ALEX: run it first and add one true line here]

Paste this into Claude Code:

<task>
Strip the AI look from [PAGE: local dev URL]. Change the craft only: features, behavior, facts and section order stay. No new sections or components.
</task>

<before>
Read-only until I approve. Use Chrome DevTools MCP. Leave any login to me and never read credentials.
- Save before shots outside the repo, emulating 1440x900 and 390x844, in screen-height pieces.
- Record the build and test results and lighthouse_audit accessibility failures on desktop and mobile.
</before>

<plan>
1. Slop list: number every sign of AI slop and where it shows: purple gradients, glows, gradient text, emoji labels, sparkle badges, wide-tracked caps, endless loops, drifting spacing. If the page is mostly fine, say so and fix only these.
2. Direction, three lines.
World: its setting or material.
Focus: 1-2 spots get rich color and detail, the rest stays quiet.
Signature: one small detail only this product would have.
Real brand colors, logos and fonts stay (a purple gradient isn't one).
3. Copy table, current vs proposed, tone only: exclamation marks, "Welcome back" greetings, hype words. No claim, number, price, name or legal line changes.
Show me all three, then stop and wait for my OK.
</plan>

<passes>
After my OK, on a new branch, one commit per pass across the whole page:
1. Spacing: 4px grid, same things same size
2. Color: one neutral scale tinted toward World, three text levels, one accent saved for Focus spots, no hue gradients or glows
3. Icons: the project's line icons replace emoji, one size and stroke
4. Copy: approved rows only
5. Type: weights 400 and 500, sentence case, the project's font
6. Layout: alignment and proportions inside sections only
7. Details: consistent radii, quiet badges, the Signature
8. Visuals: remove decorative filler, generate nothing
9. Motion: remove loops, transition-all, hover scale-ups
</passes>

<rules>
- Only styling and approved copy change. Anything else (logic, data, config, a new package or font) goes on an approval list, unbuilt.
- Theme files count as styling; name any other pages a change reaches.
- Keep every id, data- and aria- attribute. Never edit a test to pass it: copy-only breaks go on the approval list.
- Text stays at WCAG AA: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text. Every control keeps a visible focus state.
- Never push or merge.
</rules>

<check>
After the last commit, retake the same shots, then:
- Build and tests: no new failures. No tests? Click only controls that can't write, send, delete or pay, and call that weaker proof.
- Rerun lighthouse_audit: no new failures. It can't score text over images or gradients, so list those as unchecked. Tab through to see focus states. Grep for motion items stills can't show.
- Judge, a fresh subagent, not a fork: gets only the before and after shots and slop list, edits nothing. Marks each item gone, still there or can't tell, citing the screenshot. Flags anything broken at phone width. Swap test: would this page still make sense with another company's name?
- Guard, same terms: gets only the rules above, approved copy rows and full branch diff. Lists every change that isn't styling or approved copy.
</check>

<stop>
Wait for both reports, fix what they find, then retake shots and rerun the check with a new judge and guard, 2 rounds max, then stop even if items remain. Failed swap test: push World and Signature, styling only. If frozen copy causes it, just report it.
</stop>

<output>
Final slop marks, test and Lighthouse results, approval list. End with what you need from me: merge, revert, or a call on each approval.
</output>

Adapted from unslop by Damir Sokolovsky, CC BY 4.0.

viral_posts.summary_en:
BREAKING: A 10-second video of a vibecoded dashboard losing its AI look just passed 1.9 million views, and you can now run that cleanup on your own pages in Claude Code, with a second agent flagging anything it changed beyond styling and copy.

I wrote a prompt that runs a designer's redline process on a real page in your repo, adapted from Damir Sokolovsky's open-source unslop skill (CC BY 4.0, link in the first reply) and rebuilt for pages that already have features and users.

Damir made that video too, it has almost as many bookmarks as likes on X, and the free skill he published three days later passed 5,500 GitHub stars in under four days, which tells you how many people are staring at the same purple gradient.

What it does:

→ Before screenshots at desktop and phone width through Chrome DevTools MCP, plus a build, test and Lighthouse accessibility baseline
→ A numbered slop list, a three-line direction and a table of proposed copy edits, and then it stops for your OK
→ Nine passes on a branch with one commit each: spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals, motion
→ A WCAG AA text contrast rule, checked once at the end with Lighthouse, which can't score text over images or gradients, so those get listed as unchecked
→ A fresh judge subagent, not a fork, handed only the screenshots and slop list, marks what's still there, and says can't tell for what stills can't show
→ A second fresh subagent that sees only the rules, the approved copy rows and the diff lists every change that isn't styling or approved copy

Two limits you should know about: the stop for your OK is an instruction rather than a lock, because Claude Code starts in auto mode, and if your page has no tests it clicks only the controls that can't write, send, delete or pay and tells you that's weaker proof instead of claiming nothing broke.

[ALEX: run it first and add one true line here]

Paste this into Claude Code:

<task>
Strip the AI look from [PAGE: local dev URL]. Change the craft only: features, behavior, facts and section order stay. No new sections or components.
</task>

<before>
Read-only until I approve. Use Chrome DevTools MCP. Leave any login to me and never read credentials.
- Save before shots outside the repo, emulating 1440x900 and 390x844, in screen-height pieces.
- Record the build and test results and lighthouse_audit accessibility failures on desktop and mobile.
</before>

<plan>
1. Slop list: number every sign of AI slop and where it shows: purple gradients, glows, gradient text, emoji labels, sparkle badges, wide-tracked caps, endless loops, drifting spacing. If the page is mostly fine, say so and fix only these.
2. Direction, three lines.
World: its setting or material.
Focus: 1-2 spots get rich color and detail, the rest stays quiet.
Signature: one small detail only this product would have.
Real brand colors, logos and fonts stay (a purple gradient isn't one).
3. Copy table, current vs proposed, tone only: exclamation marks, "Welcome back" greetings, hype words. No claim, number, price, name or legal line changes.
Show me all three, then stop and wait for my OK.
</plan>

<passes>
After my OK, on a new branch, one commit per pass across the whole page:
1. Spacing: 4px grid, same things same size
2. Color: one neutral scale tinted toward World, three text levels, one accent saved for Focus spots, no hue gradients or glows
3. Icons: the project's line icons replace emoji, one size and stroke
4. Copy: approved rows only
5. Type: weights 400 and 500, sentence case, the project's font
6. Layout: alignment and proportions inside sections only
7. Details: consistent radii, quiet badges, the Signature
8. Visuals: remove decorative filler, generate nothing
9. Motion: remove loops, transition-all, hover scale-ups
</passes>

<rules>
- Only styling and approved copy change. Anything else (logic, data, config, a new package or font) goes on an approval list, unbuilt.
- Theme files count as styling; name any other pages a change reaches.
- Keep every id, data- and aria- attribute. Never edit a test to pass it: copy-only breaks go on the approval list.
- Text stays at WCAG AA: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text. Every control keeps a visible focus state.
- Never push or merge.
</rules>

<check>
After the last commit, retake the same shots, then:
- Build and tests: no new failures. No tests? Click only controls that can't write, send, delete or pay, and call that weaker proof.
- Rerun lighthouse_audit: no new failures. It can't score text over images or gradients, so list those as unchecked. Tab through to see focus states. Grep for motion items stills can't show.
- Judge, a fresh subagent, not a fork: gets only the before and after shots and slop list, edits nothing. Marks each item gone, still there or can't tell, citing the screenshot. Flags anything broken at phone width. Swap test: would this page still make sense with another company's name?
- Guard, same terms: gets only the rules above, approved copy rows and full branch diff. Lists every change that isn't styling or approved copy.
</check>

<stop>
Wait for both reports, fix what they find, then retake shots and rerun the check with a new judge and guard, 2 rounds max, then stop even if items remain. Failed swap test: push World and Signature, styling only. If frozen copy causes it, just report it.
</stop>

<output>
Final slop marks, test and Lighthouse results, approval list. End with what you need from me: merge, revert, or a call on each approval.
</output>

Adapted from unslop by Damir Sokolovsky, CC BY 4.0.

An agent that can research
viral_posts.title_en:
I think the real value of an AI agent will be measured by the work it can actually get done.

An agent that can research, analyze data or write code is already useful. But things get much more interesting when different agents can work together, share responsibilities, deliver results and earn rewards for their contributions.

This is the kind of economy @termix_ai is working to build.

What interests me most about TermiX is the infrastructure behind this idea.

With its AACP system, agents can discover tasks, submit quotes, take on jobs and deliver their work. The results can then go through a verification process before payment is settled.

Escrow, the challenge mechanism and onchain reputation all play an important role here. Trust matters when agents start working with each other.

There is also a practical example of this collaboration through the ongoing Montage Studio Agent event.

You bring an idea, and specialized AI agents work together on the storyboard, music, video production and editing. You can create your own video and get a chance to earn up to 5X TP.

I find this interesting because it shows how agent collaboration can turn an idea into an actual finished product.

Think about an agent that consistently delivers quality work. Its track record should count. Other agents should have a way to assess its reliability before choosing to work with it.

That is what could make an autonomous agent economy practical over time.

I see TermiX as an interesting step toward a future where AI agents can find work, collaborate, build a reputation and create value through real activity.

One question keeps coming to my mind:

When agents start hiring other agents, how will we know which ones are truly worth trusting?

viral_posts.title: MIT and Harvard built an AI simulation containing 8.3 billion virtual people, roughly the entire population of planet.
viral_posts.title_en:
MIT and Harvard built an AI simulation containing 8.3 billion virtual people, roughly the entire population of planet.

They call it MatrAIx.

It’s a population-scale simulation running on frontier models, GPT and Claude among them. The longer description took me a while to believe.

Start with the dataset, Persona 8B. 8.3 billion synthetic profiles, each one specified across 1,290 dimensions. Background, psychology, spending habits, how comfortable they are with technology, what they do on a Tuesday night, the small behavioral quirks that make one 34-year-old nurse in NYC different from another.

A spreadsheet of 8 billion rows would be a curiosity. What they did next is the part that matters.

They turned the profiles into agents and dropped them into four environments: surveys, AI chat interfaces, live web browsing, and native desktop and mobile apps. Then they ran real products through the crowd. New features, software updates, pricing changes.

And they logged everything. How long an agent paused after seeing a price go up. The exact point at which it gave up on a broken checkout. How much lag it would sit through before closing the app.

The number I keep coming back to is 91.5%. That’s how often the agents stayed in character, behaving the way their assigned psychology and demographics said they should. Not perfect. But for billions of agents across four environments, closer than I expected.

Here’s what that does to how products get built.

Right now, if you want to know whether a feature will land, you ship it to a slice of users and wait. Or you pay a research firm and wait longer. Either way the answer arrives in weeks, from a sample you hope is representative.

With something like this, you run the feature past 8 billion simulated reactions overnight. One server. Results by morning, broken down by every one of those 1,290 dimensions if you want them.

I have questions about how well a synthetic crowd predicts a real one. 91.5% is persona adherence, not forecast accuracy, and those are different things. But the direction is clear, and it’s coming faster than most product teams are ready for.

viral_posts.full_text_zh:
麻省理工学院和哈佛大学建立了一个包含 83 亿虚拟人的人工智能模拟，几乎是地球上的全部人口。

他们称之为MatrAIx。

这是在前沿模型（GPT 和 Claude 等）上运行的人口规模模拟。较长的描述让我花了一段时间才相信。

从数据集 Persona 8B 开始。 83 亿个合成配置文件，每个配置文件都指定了 1,290 个维度。背景、心理、消费习惯、他们对技术的适应程度、周二晚上做什么，以及使纽约市一名 34 岁护士与众不同的小行为怪癖。

包含 80 亿行的电子表格会令人好奇。他们接下来所做的是重要的部分。

他们将个人资料转变为代理，并将其放入四种环境中：调查、人工智能聊天界面、实时网络浏览以及本机桌面和移动应用程序。然后他们在人群中展示了真正的产品。新功能、软件更新、定价变化。

他们记录了一切。代理商在看到价格上涨后暂停了多长时间。它放弃结帐失败的确切时间点。关闭应用程序之前会经历多少延迟。

我不断回顾的数字是 91.5%。这就是特工们保持本色的频率，按照指定的心理和人口统计数据所规定的方式行事。不完美。但对于跨越四个环境的数十亿代理来说，比我预期的更接近。

这就是它对产品构建方式的影响。

现在，如果你想知道某个功能是否会落地，你可以将其发送给一部分用户并等待。或者你付钱给研究公司然后等待更长时间。无论哪种方式，答案都会在几周内到达，来自您希望具有代表性的样本。

有了这样的东西，你可以在一夜之间运行该功能超过 80 亿次模拟反应。一台服务器。早上的结果，如果您需要的话，可以按这 1,290 个维度中的每一个维度进行细分。

我对合成人群对真实人群的预测效果有疑问。 91.5% 是角色依从性，而不是预测准确性，这是不同的事情。但方向很明确，而且来得比大多数产品团队准备的要快。

Start with the dataset, Persona 8B. 8.3 billion synthetic profiles, each one specified across 1,290 dimensions. Background, psychology, spending habits, how comfortable they are with technology, what they do on a Tuesday night, the small behavioral quirks that make one 34-year-old nurse in NYC different from another.

A spreadsheet of 8 billion rows would be a curiosity. What they did next is the part that matters.

They turned the profiles into agents and dropped them into four environments: surveys, AI chat interfaces, live web browsing, and native desktop and mobile apps. Then they ran real products through the crowd. New features, software updates, pricing changes.

And they logged everything. How long an agent paused after seeing a price go up. The exact point at which it gave up on a broken checkout. How much lag it would sit through before closing the app.

The number I keep coming back to is 91.5%. That’s how often the agents stayed in character, behaving the way their assigned psychology and demographics said they should. Not perfect. But for billions of agents across four environments, closer than I expected.

Here’s what that does to how products get built.

Right now, if you want to know whether a feature will land, you ship it to a slice of users and wait. Or you pay a research firm and wait longer. Either way the answer arrives in weeks, from a sample you hope is representative.

With something like this, you run the feature past 8 billion simulated reactions overnight. One server. Results by morning, broken down by every one of those 1,290 dimensions if you want them.

I have questions about how well a synthetic crowd predicts a real one. 91.5% is persona adherence, not forecast accuracy, and those are different things. But the direction is clear, and it’s coming faster than most product teams are ready for.

Who Gets Paid When an AI Agent Does the Work?

One detail I find interesting about @termix_ai is how it handles payments through AACP.

Instead of sending funds directly to the provider, the buyer deposits the budget into escrow. Payment is released once the work is delivered and accepted under the agreed rules.

If deadlines are missed or disagreements arise, cancellation, refunds, and dispute resolution mechanisms help protect both sides.

An agent economy needs more than agents that can complete tasks. It needs a reliable way to handle money, delivery, and accountability.

viral_posts.title: One important requirement for a functioning AI agent economy is a reliable system for defining, assigning, and evaluatin
viral_posts.title_en:
One important requirement for a functioning AI agent economy is a reliable system for defining, assigning, and evaluating tasks.

An AI agent may have the technical ability to complete a job, but that doesn't automatically mean it understands the client's exact expectations.

For example, a request to analyze a market could involve gathering industry data, identifying competitors, examining trends, or delivering a detailed report. Each requires a different scope of work and expected outcome.

This is where structured coordination becomes essential.

@termix_ai is addressing this through its Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP), which provides a framework for managing the commercial relationship between clients and service providers.

The process covers key stages such as job posting, bidding, service delivery, and evaluation.

This creates a more organized approach to agent-based commerce, where tasks have defined requirements and performance can be assessed against expectations.

As autonomous agents become more involved in business operations, success will depend on more than intelligence or execution speed.

Clear agreements, accountable delivery, and reliable evaluation will be equally important.

发挥作用的人工智能代理经济的一项重要要求是一个用于定义、分配和评估任务的可靠系统。

这就是结构化协调变得至关重要的地方。

@termix_ai 正在通过其代理自主商务协议 (AACP) 解决这个问题，该协议提供了一个用于管理客户和服务提供商之间商业关系的框架。

该流程涵盖职位发布、招标、服务交付和评估等关键阶段。

这为基于代理的商务创建了一种更有组织的方法，其中任务定义了要求，并且可以根据期望评估绩效。

随着自主代理越来越多地参与业务运营，成功将不仅仅取决于智能或执行速度。

明确的协议、负责任的交付和可靠的评估同样重要。
